film_list.synopsis: Mommy issues abound in Filip Anthonissen’s uniquely unsettling 3D animation, a surreal and sharply comedic Oedipal odyssey in which a middle-aged manchild traverses bucolic goat fields, pounding raves, and a pagan cult in his quest to mollify his overbearing mother.

film_list.title: Koden'n
film_list.synopsis: When Western medicine fails to explain a couple’s multiple miscarriages, a husband turns to his Haitian ancestry for solutions in Daniel «Tètèl» Chérubin’s restrained and mood-driven horror that leans on the importance of inherited spiritual traditions.

film_list.title: MAMMALIA
film_list.synopsis: With meticulous precision, Elia Kalogianni excavates the fissure between care and abuse in a visually stunning and wildly depraved film about two sadistic women who stage experiments and lessons in abject cruelty in their battle for dominance.

film_list.title: Into The Betaverse
film_list.synopsis: A virtual identity crisis meets dank British comedy in Varun Raman and Tom Hancock’s satirical take on the pressures of class and masculinity, and the value of homosocial friendship.

film_list.title: Madrugada
film_list.synopsis: When their young son begins to experience destructive desires, a vampiric father and human mother try to shield him from blood-soaked nocturnal exploits in Sebastián Lojo’s slow-burn rumination on generational malaise.

film_list.title: The Dream Is A Snail
film_list.synopsis: Thien An Nguyen’s highly stylized, eccentric comedy follows a desperate background actor who finds his calling by offering his body as a snail race host and discovers a world of erotic delights in sensations elicited by his slimy new friends.

film_list.synopsis: A pickpocket’s affairs come to a head when he’s entrusted with looking after his spirited younger cousin while scrambling to settle a debt with his soon-to-be ex-girlfriend, in Romain F. Dubois’ zesty winner of the Sony Discovery Prize at the 2026 Cannes Critics’ Week.

film_list.title: Untitled Woman
film_list.synopsis: A magnificent Julianne Nicholson plays a middle-aged woman longing to be seen in Camille Summers-Valli’s elegant, meticulously composed character study set at an art class with a charismatic teacher (Charles Melton) and a delightful group of eccentrics eager to gaze.

film_list.title: When the Ground Paused
film_list.synopsis: Jess Barclay Lawton’s achingly raw documentary is a deeply affecting snapshot of early motherhood in which a young woman reflects on childhood scars in an effort to become the nurturing, attentive mother she longed to have.

film_list.title: The End
film_list.synopsis: Winner of the 2017 Best International Short Film (The Burden), Niki Lindroth von Bahr returns to TIFF with another brilliant stop-motion doomsday comedy, in which airport-bound creatures wait out the impending apocalypse. Featuring voices by Alexander Skarsgård, Denis Lavant, and Noomi Rapace.

film_list.title: The Highway
film_list.synopsis: Yung Chang, one of Canada’s most prominent documentary filmmakers, makes a haunting narrative debut with this visually arresting, atmospheric slow-burner about an affluent businesswoman whose cushy routine and sense of reality unravel after she drives past the aftermath of a hit and run.

film_list.title: Fried Chicken & Strip Checkers
film_list.synopsis: A brother and sister at odds over household responsibilities are in for a dose of the bigger picture when a visit to their father in prison opens their eyes to the dark cloud hanging over their family’s future, in Ophelia Harutyunyan’s richly textured sibling drama.

film_list.synopsis: An unspeakable act of cruelty on an idyllic summer night disrupts and forever changes a young boy and his sister’s understanding of the world in Julie Charette’s deeply moving animated drama that so vividly evokes a sense of summer air tinged with heartbreak.

film_list.title: Termite

film_list.title: The Lion Does Not Concern Himself
film_list.synopsis: Zarrar Kahn’s latest is a charming romantic comedy about an endearing gym coach who is convinced that his online persona as a toxic podcaster is his only ticket to relevance and popularity until a new client and love interest enters his life.

films.title: Zjili: A Story of Sisterhood and The Burdens of Excess
films.genre: Directed by Women, First Feature, Black + African Diaspora, Drama
films.synopsis: In their poignant debut feature, co-directors Christine Boateng and Hajara Musah Chambas depict the journey of three Ghanaian women eking out a living as kayayei or porters in the trenches of the world’s largest secondhand clothing market.
